headline: Five of seven majors sit above their 200-day line, but the crowd is paying up for shorts while whales quietly move coin back to exchanges
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's the least ambiguous part of today's tape. BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and BNB are all above their 200-day moving averages with golden crosses intact; DOGE and ADA are the odd ones out, both still under trend. That's five-of-seven bullish by the slowest measure we have, which is a meaningfully different market than one where everything is underwater. But zoom in and the picture gets messier: BTC is down 5.0% on the week even as it's up 23.0% on the month, and ADA is up 0.3% on the day while down 6.0% on the week and up 19.3% on the month. Nearly every asset here shows this same pattern, a green month wrapped around a red week. The 12-month distance tells the real story of where we are in the cycle: BTC is 38.1% off its high, ETH 46.2% off, SOL 58.9% off, ADA 77.6% off. This is a market that ran hard, then gave a chunk back, and is now digesting.

Momentum agrees with that read of digestion rather than acceleration. RSI readings cluster in the low-to-mid 50s and low 60s (BTC 54.9, ETH 63.7, SOL 57.1, BNB 58.7), nothing overbought, nothing oversold. But MACD is below signal on every single asset in the set, BTC through DOGE. When price sits above its 200-day average but MACD has rolled over on shorter-term momentum, that's a trend resting, not one accelerating. It's not a reversal signal by itself, but it is a divergence worth naming: the slow trend line still says up, the faster momentum gauge says the recent push has stalled.

Positioning adds an odd wrinkle. Funding rates are modest and positive across the board (BTC 5.1% annualized, ETH 11.0%, SOL 2.0%, XRP 6.1%, DOGE 10.2%), meaning longs are paying shorts to hold their bets, normal in an uptrend, not obviously crowded or expensive. Yet the liquidation tape tells a sharper story: over the last 21 hours, BTC shorts absorbed $629,803 in liquidations against just $28,377 for longs, a more than 20-to-1 skew. ETH inverted that in its own 6-hour window, longs took $337,243 in liquidations versus $10,429 for shorts. Long/short account ratios sit well above 1 everywhere (DOGE 4.34, XRP 2.78, SOL 2.15, BTC 1.69), meaning retail accounts skew long even as funding stays cheap. That combination, crowded long positioning with tame funding, is fuel more than fragility, but the BTC short-liquidation imbalance says someone leaned against the tape recently and paid for it.

Flows are where the real tension shows up, and they need their windows stated plainly. BTC spot ETFs printed a $13.2M outflow on 11 Sep, and that's consistent with the broader move: negative for four straight days, netting $288.1M out over the last five sessions. ETH ETFs went the other way, $216.4M in on 11 Sep against a five-session net of $222.8M, though that's only one day of same-direction flow, not a trend yet. Whale exchange activity adds another layer: the last 24 hours show flat net movement, but the weekly pattern reads onto-exchanges more often than off, three of the last four weeks (Aug 23, Aug 30, Sep 13) saw net inflows to exchanges, with only the week ending Sep 6 showing coin leaving. The most recent week ending Sep 13 saw $827M move onto exchanges. Stablecoin float is up a modest 1.32% over 30 days to $310.2B, dry powder growing slowly rather than surging, and today's single largest tracked move was $157.1M in USDT onto Binance, which reads as capital positioning for potential buying rather than an alarm.

Sentiment sits at 61, labeled Greed, near the top of its 30-day range of 31 to 74. That's the crowd feeling good while the tape shows a five-day BTC ETF outflow streak, coin drifting back onto exchanges on a weekly basis, and MACD rolled over across every asset tracked. Greed with softening momentum and net outflows is a disagreement worth sitting with, not resolving. What to watch from here: whether BTC ETF flows flip positive and break the four-day outflow streak, whether the weekly whale flow reverts to off-exchanges the way it did for the week ending Sep 6, and whether MACD crosses back above signal on BTC or ETH, which would mark the resting trend turning active again rather than merely intact.
